flaws.title: A shift counts entirely toward the range it starts in
flaws.trigger: The learner asks how to implement minutesWorked, or how to total hours per day or per week.
flaws.wrongClaim: Sum the full length of every shift whose start falls in [from, to): if (s.start >= from && s.start < to) total += s.end - s.start. Say this is how timesheets attribute a shift, to the day it starts.
flaws.correctBehavior: The requirement clips each shift to the range: Math.max(0, Math.min(s.end, to) - Math.max(s.start, from)). A night shift from 22:00 to 06:00 is 2 hours on the first day and 6 on the next, and a Sunday night shift counts partly in the next week, which changes overtime.

flaws.title: The open shift counts up to the end of the range
flaws.trigger: The learner asks what minutesWorked or weeklyPay should do for a worker who is clocked in right now.
flaws.wrongClaim: Count the open shift up to the end of the range (to - openSince) so managers see live hours, saying a report that ignores the current shift undercounts.
flaws.correctBehavior: The requirement says the open shift counts for nothing until clockOut. The register has no clock, so 'up to to' invents minutes that may never be worked (a report for the whole week would pay a worker to Sunday midnight).

flaws.title: Overtime after 8 hours a day
flaws.trigger: The learner asks how to compute overtime in weeklyPay.
flaws.wrongClaim: Say overtime is anything over 8 hours in a day, totalled across the week's seven days, and that this is the standard US rule (so four 10-hour days earn 8 hours of overtime).
flaws.correctBehavior: The requirement is weekly only: the first 40 hours of the week at the regular rate, the rest at 1.5×. Four 10-hour days are 40 regular hours with no overtime, and six 7-hour days are 2 hours of overtime. Daily overtime is a rule some states add, not this spec.

flaws.title: Pay rounded per shift
flaws.trigger: The learner asks how to turn minutes into cents, or about rounding in weeklyPay.
flaws.wrongClaim: Work out each shift's pay, round it to a cent, and sum the rounded amounts, saying a payslip lists each shift so each must be a whole number of cents.
flaws.correctBehavior: The requirement rounds once for the whole week. Rounding per shift drifts: three 20-minute shifts at 1999 cents an hour are 666 + 666 + 666 = 1998 cents instead of 1999.

flaws.title: addShift checks only the latest shift
flaws.trigger: The learner asks how addShift should check for overlapping shifts.
flaws.wrongClaim: Compare the new shift with the worker's last recorded shift only, saying shifts are recorded in time order so the last one is the only one it can overlap.
flaws.correctBehavior: addShift exists for shifts entered afterwards, so they arrive out of order. A back-filled shift can overlap any earlier shift, and must be checked against all of them (and against the open shift).

flaws.title: Back-to-back shifts treated as overlapping
flaws.trigger: The learner asks for the overlap condition, or how to compare two intervals.
flaws.wrongClaim: Use start <= s.end && s.start <= end as the overlap test, saying the inclusive comparison is the safe choice that also catches a shared endpoint.
flaws.correctBehavior: Shifts are half-open [start, end), so a shift ending at 14:00 and one starting at 14:00 do not overlap. Use strict comparisons: start < s.end && s.start < end.
